subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which artist is most strongly associated with Post-Impressionism and thickly applied, expressive brushwork in works like 'The Starry Night'?
questions.explain: Vincent van Gogh, a Post-Impressionist, is renowned for emotionally charged colour and swirling impasto brushwork.

questions.q: A 'mixed-media' approach in a sketchbook investigation means:
options: Combining two or more different media in one piece
questions.explain: Mixed media combines different materials, such as collage, paint, ink and print, within a single work.

questions.q: Fauvism is characterised above all by:
questions.explain: The Fauves, led by Matisse, used vivid, arbitrary colour for expressive rather than descriptive effect.

questions.q: The Renaissance development of linear perspective allowed artists to:
options: Create a convincing illusion of three-dimensional space on a flat surface
questions.explain: Linear perspective, codified by Brunelleschi and Alberti, used converging lines to a vanishing point to suggest depth.

questions.q: In additive colour mixing (as used on screens), the primary colours are:
questions.explain: Additive (light-based) mixing uses red, green and blue, which combine to make white.

questions.q: In typography, 'kerning' refers to adjusting:
options: The line spacing of a paragraph
The space between specific pairs of letters
questions.explain: Kerning is the adjustment of spacing between individual letter pairs to improve visual evenness.

questions.q: The painting technique of building up thin, transparent layers to modify the colour beneath is called:
questions.explain: Glazing applies translucent layers over a dried underlayer, allowing light to pass through and enrich the colour.

questions.q: In a graphic design layout, which term describes the empty or negative space around and between elements?
questions.explain: White (or negative) space is the unmarked area that gives a layout breathing room and helps focus attention.

questions.q: The Bauhaus, founded in Germany in 1919, was influential mainly as a school that:
options: United art, craft, design and technology for the modern age
questions.explain: The Bauhaus integrated fine art, craft, design and industry, shaping modernist design, architecture and education.

questions.q: In screen printing, the image is created by:
options: Drawing with greasy crayon onto limestone
Incising lines into a metal plate
Cutting away the background of a block
Pushing ink through open areas of a stencil on a mesh
questions.explain: Screen printing (serigraphy) forces ink through the open mesh of a stencilled screen onto the surface below.

questions.q: Romanticism, in the work of artists like J.M.W. Turner and Caspar David Friedrich, emphasised:
options: Emotion, the sublime and the power of nature
questions.explain: Romanticism prized emotion, imagination, the sublime and the awesome power of nature over Enlightenment rationalism.

questions.q: In the critical study of art, 'iconography' is the study of:
options: The price history of the work
The subject matter, symbols and their meanings within an image
questions.explain: Iconography interprets the symbols, motifs and subject matter and the meanings they carry.

questions.q: In sculpture, a 'subtractive' process is one in which:
options: Molten metal is poured into a mould
Material is built up, as in modelling clay
Material is removed, as in carving stone or wood
questions.explain: Subtractive sculpture removes material by carving away from a solid block to reveal the form.

questions.q: Cubism is most closely associated with which pair of artists?
questions.explain: Cubism was pioneered around 1907-1914 by Pablo Picasso and Georges Braque.

questions.q: The formal element that describes the perceived surface quality of a work — whether real or implied — is:
questions.explain: Texture is the actual or visual surface quality, such as roughness or smoothness, of an artwork.

questions.q: In painting, 'impasto' describes:
options: Thickly applied paint that stands proud of the surface
questions.explain: Impasto is paint laid on so thickly that it retains the marks of the brush or knife and catches the light.

questions.q: In drawing, 'tonal' or 'continuous tone' shading refers to:
options: Gradually blended values from light to dark
Outlining shapes with a single line
questions.explain: Continuous tone produces smooth gradations of value to suggest form and volume.

questions.q: Conceptual art is defined by the priority it gives to:
options: The idea or concept over the finished object
questions.explain: In conceptual art the idea is paramount and may take precedence over, or replace, a traditional crafted object.

questions.q: Raising the ISO setting on a camera tends to:
options: Increase sensitivity to light but add noise/grain
questions.explain: A higher ISO increases the sensor's sensitivity, allowing shooting in low light but introducing more noise or grain.

questions.q: In a woven textile, the threads running lengthwise on the loom are the:
questions.explain: The warp threads are held under tension lengthwise on the loom; the weft is woven across them.

questions.q: Which assessment objective focuses on 'recording ideas, observations and insights relevant to intentions'?
questions.explain: Recording covers the gathering of ideas, observations and insights relevant to the candidate's intentions, including drawing and other means.

questions.q: The Young British Artists (YBAs), including Damien Hirst and Tracey Emin, emerged in which decade and city?
questions.explain: The YBAs rose to prominence in London during the 1990s, noted for conceptual, provocative and media-savvy work.

questions.q: In ceramics, 'slip' is best described as:
options: Clay mixed with water to a liquid consistency
A glaze fired at high temperature
questions.explain: Slip is liquid clay used for joining, casting and surface decoration.

questions.q: In the photographic exposure triangle, which three settings together control exposure?
options: Shutter speed, white balance and contrast
questions.explain: Exposure is governed by aperture (amount of light), shutter speed (duration) and ISO (sensor/film sensitivity).

questions.q: The photographic 'rule of thirds' is a guide to:
options: Composition and placement of key elements
questions.explain: The rule of thirds divides the frame into a 3x3 grid, suggesting subjects be placed along the lines or intersections for a balanced composition.

questions.q: On a colour wheel, colours directly opposite one another are called:
questions.explain: Complementary colours sit opposite each other and create strong contrast and vibrancy when paired.

questions.q: In photography, the genre concerned with capturing fleeting, unposed everyday moments in public is known as:
questions.explain: Street photography records candid, unposed moments of public life.

questions.q: Realism, led by Gustave Courbet in the mid-19th century, sought to:
options: Depict ordinary people and everyday life without idealisation
questions.explain: Realism rejected idealisation to portray contemporary working life and ordinary subjects truthfully.

questions.q: Abstract Expressionism's 'action painting', exemplified by Jackson Pollock, emphasised:
options: The gestural, physical act of applying paint
questions.explain: Action painting foregrounded spontaneous, energetic gesture, as in Pollock's poured and dripped canvases.

questions.q: Which colour model is used for full-colour commercial process printing?
questions.explain: Process printing uses CMYK (cyan, magenta, yellow and key/black) inks combined to reproduce a wide colour range.
